chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me from his uncle Muhammad ibn Abi al-Qasim, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Kufi, from Nasr ibn Muzahim, from Lut ibn Yahya, from al-Harith ibn Ka'b, from Fatima bint Ali (blessings of God be upon them both):

Then Yazid (may God curse him) ordered that the women of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) be imprisoned with Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) in a prison that had no protection from heat or cold, until their faces peeled.

Not a stone was raised from the face of the earth in Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) except that fresh blood was found beneath it. And the people saw the sun on the walls appearing red, as though it were sheets dyed with safflower.
until Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) was released with the women, and the head of al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was returned to Karbala.

key_terms.الملاحف المعصفرة: Safflower-dyed sheets — a vivid metaphor for the blood-red sunlight that appeared on walls as a cosmic sign of grief
key_terms.بيت المقدس: Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) — the holy site where miraculous signs appeared after the martyrdom of Husayn
key_terms.دم عبيط: Fresh blood — a sign of divine mourning appearing supernaturally under stones in Jerusalem
key_terms.محبس: Prison, place of confinement — referring to the jail where Husayn's family was held in Damascus

ai.seo_question: What happened to the family of Imam Husayn after the Battle of Karbala?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by Fatima bint Ali, an eyewitness to the aftermath of the Battle of Karbala (61 AH), describes the cruel imprisonment of Imam Husayn's family by Yazid ibn Mu'awiya in a prison exposed to extreme weather. It also recounts supernatural signs of cosmic mourning: fresh blood appearing beneath every stone lifted in Jerusalem, and the sun casting a blood-red light on walls resembling safflower-dyed sheets. The account concludes with the eventual release of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (Zayn al-Abidin) with the women and the return of Imam Husayn's head to Karbala.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated this to us from his uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim from Muhammad b. `Ali al-Kufi from Nasr b. Mazahim from Lut b. Yahya from al-Harith b. Ka`b from Fatima bt.
`Ali (s). Yazid (la) called for the women of al-Husayn (as) to be jailed with `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) in a jail that had no protection from heat or cold, until their faces peeled.

A stone from the face of the Earth was not raised in the Bayt al-Maqdis except that fresh blood was found beneath it. The people saw red sunlight on the walls, as though it were sheets dyed in yellow;
until `Ali b. al-Husayn (as) was released with the women and the head of al-Husayn (as) was returned to Karbala’.
